dimensions.assessment: Affects specific political and economic elites in Haiti, gang members, and designated foreign persons, along with U.S. federal agency personnel involved in reporting and enforcement.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 90 days after the date the report required by section 2 is submitted... the President shall impose sanctions

dimensions.assessment: Imposes significant penalties on targeted individuals, including property blocking in the United States, visa revocations, and inadmissibility.
dimensions.evidence: block and prohibit all transactions in all property and interests in property of any foreign person

dimensions.assessment: The source does not detail specific direct appropriations or federal spending amounts, focusing instead on reporting and sanctions mandates.
Mandates multi-agency federal reporting and the imposition of specific property and visa sanctions under modified IEEPA and immigration authorities.
dimensions.evidence: the President shall impose sanctions described in subsection (b) with respect to each foreign person identified

dimensions.assessment: The act contains a strict 5-year sunset provision ending all force and effect 5 years after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: This Act shall cease to have any force or effect beginning on the date that is 5 years after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific figures on federal spending or budgetary appropriations required to implement the reporting and sanctions.
The exact number of individuals who will be identified or subjected to sanctions.
importance_detail.rationale: S. 1854 requires reports and sanctions on specific political and economic elites and gangs in Haiti, affecting foreign individuals, bilateral relations, and U.S. immigration and property blocking authorities for a limited 5-year period.
